claims.text: Local chemical-environment variations in high-entropy alloy superconductors soften specific low-energy phonon modes.
Softening of low-energy phonon modes enhances electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling facilitates Cooper-pair formation and thereby governs superconductivity in these HEAs.
(TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 is a body-centered-cubic, highly disordered HEA displaying robust superconductivity at cryogenic temperatures.
Heat treatment can reduce local chemical disorder in the same HEA composition.
The random distribution of multiple principal elements creates local structural fluctuations and spatial variations in bonding and lattice vibrations.
Favorable disorder-generated local bonding configurations selectively soften low-energy phonon modes.
Reducing local disorder should diminish low-energy phonon softening.
Changing the degree of disorder can alter superconducting properties such as Tc.
More highly disordered samples should exhibit stronger low-energy phonon softening than heat-treated, less-disordered samples.
Stronger phonon softening should correlate with a robust superconducting gap and a higher or more resilient Tc.
A lower-entropy or more crystalline analogue should exhibit less phonon-mode softening and different superconducting transition behavior.
The proposed mechanism applies primarily to significantly disordered HEAs in which phonon-mediated pairing is dominant.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate in BCC or layered HEA structures near the superconducting transition.
Magnetic interactions can weaken or override conventional phonon-mediated superconductivity.
Extreme spin-orbit coupling can override the proposed electron-phonon mechanism.
Electron count and degree of disorder are additional parameters that can affect superconductivity in HEAs.
Configurational entropy and short-range atomic order can potentially be tuned to improve superconducting performance.
Neutron scattering can measure phonon dispersion, while ARPES and muon spin rotation can characterize electronic or superconducting behavior.
Similar measured disorder, phonon spectra, and superconducting behavior in the as-cast and heat-treated samples would falsify the proposed disorder-driven mechanism.
